stacks.label: Node.js / JavaScript / TypeScript
stacks.coreLayer: src/services + src/lib - pure modules testable without HTTP or UI
conventions: ESM (`"type": "module"`) unless the toolchain forces CJS
TypeScript strict; never reach for `any` as a shortcut

stacks.label: Deno
stacks.coreLayer: src/ pure modules; explicit permission flags, never `-A` in production
conventions: Import through the `deno.json` imports map, not bare URLs scattered in files

stacks.label: Bun
stacks.coreLayer: src/services - pure modules kept apart from the server entrypoint
conventions: Use the built-in `bun test`; do not add a second runner without a reason
bun has no `--if-present`, so the npm idiom for an optional script does not port — name your real commands in `vibe.gates` instead of relying on a no-op
`bun test` exits 1 on "No tests found!", like pytest and unlike `cargo test` or `go test` — a new Bun project's test gate is red until the first *.test.ts exists

stacks.label: Python
stacks.coreLayer: pure domain packages (services/, domain/) - I/O at the edges, not inside the logic
conventions: Type hints on every public function
Manage dependencies in pyproject.toml, not a hand-edited requirements.txt

`pytest` exits 5 when it collects nothing, so the test gate is red until the first test exists — `cargo test` and `npm run test --if-present` pass vacuously, this does not. Write a test rather than weakening the gate
pytest only discovers `test_*.py` / `*_test.py`; a file named `tests_foo.py` is silently ignored

stacks.label: PHP
stacks.coreLayer: app/Services + app/Domain - controllers only parse input and delegate
conventions: PSR-12 formatting
`declare(strict_types=1);` in every file

stacks.label: Go
stacks.coreLayer: internal/ - domain packages; cmd/ is wiring only
conventions: Standard layout: cmd/, internal/, pkg/
Wrap errors with `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)`; never swallow them

Detection reads go.mod as text, and go.mod lists `// indirect` dependencies too — a framework that embeds another (Wails vendors labstack/echo) can be mis-detected. Give your entry more signals so the specific evidence outranks the incidental

stacks.label: Rust
stacks.coreLayer: the crate's lib.rs / domain modules - the binary stays a thin shell
conventions: `Result<T, E>` with your own error type (thiserror); `unwrap()` is banned on production paths
`cargo fmt` before committing

stacks.label: Java / Kotlin (Maven)
stacks.coreLayer: service/domain packages - controllers stay thin
conventions: Constructor injection, never field injection

stacks.label: Java / Kotlin (Gradle)
stacks.coreLayer: a domain module kept separate from the app module
conventions: Version catalog (`gradle/libs.versions.toml`) for dependencies

stacks.label: .NET / C#
stacks.coreLayer: the Application/Domain project - the Web/UI project is presentation only
conventions: Nullable reference types enabled
async/await all the way down; avoid `.Result`
`dotnet format --verify-no-changes` fails (exit 2) on freshly generated `dotnet new` output, so it is not a default gate here — add it once your own code is formatted

stacks.label: Ruby
stacks.coreLayer: app/services (service objects) - models do not hold orchestration
conventions: Follow the project's rubocop config; do not disable a cop without a written reason

stacks.label: Elixir
stacks.coreLayer: context modules - not controllers or LiveViews
conventions: One context per domain; the web layer never calls Repo directly

stacks.label: Dart
stacks.coreLayer: lib/src/ pure domain modules
conventions: `dart format .` before committing

stacks.label: Swift
stacks.coreLayer: Sources/<Core> - a target separate from the App target
conventions: Release version (MARKETING_VERSION) is set by hand in Xcode - see docs/VERSIONING.md
SwiftLint is a separate install, not part of the toolchain — `swiftlint` exits 127 on a stock machine, so it is not a default gate here; add it to `vibe.gates` once you have installed it
`swift test` exits 1 when the package has no test target at all — `swift package init --type executable` creates none, so add a Tests/ target before expecting a green test gate

stacks.label: C / C++ (CMake)
stacks.coreLayer: the library target - the executable is wiring only
conventions: Turn on warnings-as-errors in CI
`cmake -B build` must run before anything else — a fresh clone has no build directory, which is why the typecheck gate configures as well as compiles

stacks.label: Electron (desktop)
stacks.coreLayer: the main process (Node) - the renderer is pure presentation; all FS/DB/child-process work lives in main
conventions: `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`; the only bridge is a preload contextBridge
Validate every IPC payload in main - the renderer is untrusted
Never load remote content into a window that has preload access
This template sets `"type": "module"`, so name main and preload `.cjs` — an ESM preload additionally needs `sandbox: false` and Electron >= 28
`npm run gate` runs your `build` script: point it at electron-builder/Forge, or at minimum a smoke launch that boots main + preload + renderer

stacks.label: Tauri (desktop, Rust + web)
stacks.coreLayer: Rust in src-tauri/src - the frontend only calls `#[tauri::command]` and holds no heavy logic
conventions: Every Rust command validates its own arguments; the frontend is untrusted
Keep the tauri.conf.json allowlist/capabilities as narrow as possible
Heavy work goes in an `async` command or a thread - never block the main thread
`src-tauri/icons/icon.ico` is REQUIRED on Windows — tauri-build fails the whole compile without it, long before any of your code is checked
The first `npm run gate` compiles the entire Rust dependency tree (several minutes); it is not hung

stacks.label: Wails (desktop, Go + web)
stacks.coreLayer: the bound Go structs - the frontend calls them instead of duplicating logic
conventions: Bound methods return explicit errors; never panic across the bridge

`frontend/dist` is gitignored but `go:embed` needs it — on a fresh clone `go vet`, `go build` and `go test` ALL fail until something builds the frontend, which is why the typecheck gate runs `wails build -nopackage` first
Wails v2 vendors labstack/echo, so a plain substring match on go.mod would detect this project as Echo; the entry carries three signals so the specific evidence wins

stacks.label: .NET MAUI (desktop/mobile)
stacks.coreLayer: the ViewModel/Services project - XAML code-behind stays empty
conventions: Strict MVVM; bind, do not manipulate controls directly

stacks.label: Avalonia UI (desktop)
stacks.coreLayer: the ViewModel/Services project - the View is XAML only
conventions: MVVM via ReactiveUI or CommunityToolkit.Mvvm - pick one and stay consistent

stacks.label: Next.js
stacks.coreLayer: Server Components / Route Handlers / server actions - Client Components are presentation only
conventions: `"use client"` as rarely and as close to the leaves as possible
Fetch data on the server; never have the server call its own API over HTTP
Secrets stay in server-only env vars (no `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix)

stacks.label: Nuxt
stacks.coreLayer: server/api + server/utils (Nitro) - client composables stay thin
conventions: `useFetch`/`useAsyncData` for data, not bare `fetch` in setup
`runtimeConfig` for secrets; `public` only for what is safe to expose

stacks.label: React + Vite
stacks.coreLayer: src/services + src/hooks - components hold no business logic
conventions: Function components and hooks; no new class components
Server state via TanStack Query, not hand-rolled useEffect

stacks.label: Vue 3 + Vite
stacks.coreLayer: src/composables + src/services - SFCs stay presentational
conventions: `<script setup>` with the Composition API
Pinia for global state, never an event bus

stacks.label: Angular
stacks.coreLayer: Injectable services - components only orchestrate the view
conventions: Standalone components for new code
RxJS: always unsubscribe (takeUntilDestroyed) - a leaked subscription is a bug
OnPush change detection by default
Angular 20+ runs tests on Vitest, not Karma: `--browsers=ChromeHeadless` now demands a separate @vitest/browser-* provider and fails without one. `ng test --watch=false` is the portable form

stacks.label: SvelteKit
stacks.coreLayer: `+page.server.ts` / `src/lib/server` - secrets must never leave `$lib/server`
conventions: `load` for data; forms use actions, not manual fetch
Nothing in `$lib/server` can reach the client bundle - rely on that

stacks.label: Astro
stacks.coreLayer: `.astro` components render on the server - client islands are for interactivity only
conventions: Keep islands minimal; every `client:*` directive is a deliberate choice

stacks.label: Remix / React Router 7
stacks.coreLayer: `loader`/`action` in the route module - components just render the result
conventions: Progressive enhancement: forms must still work with JS disabled

stacks.label: SolidStart
stacks.coreLayer: server functions (`"use server"`) - components stay thin
conventions: Fine-grained signals; do not import React re-render habits
SolidStart v2 builds with Vite + Nitro and emits `.output/`; `.vinxi/` is a v1 artefact, kept in the ignore list for older projects

stacks.label: Express
stacks.coreLayer: src/services + src/repositories - route handlers only validate, delegate and serialise
conventions: One central error-handling middleware; no try/catch scattered per route
Validate input at the boundary (zod/joi) before it reaches a service

stacks.label: NestJS
stacks.coreLayer: providers/services per module - controllers are thin and hold no business logic
conventions: One module per domain; wire dependencies through DI, not direct imports
DTOs plus a global ValidationPipe for all input
A repository layer keeps the ORM out of your services

stacks.label: Fastify
stacks.coreLayer: src/services - route handlers are adapters only
conventions: A JSON Schema per route (validation plus fast serialisation) - this is why you chose Fastify
Wrap cross-route concerns as plugins instead of registering globals ad hoc

stacks.label: Hono
stacks.coreLayer: runtime-agnostic service modules - handlers sit thinly on top
conventions: Stay on Web standards (Request/Response) so the code stays portable across runtimes
`@hono/zod-validator` at the input boundary

stacks.label: AdonisJS
stacks.coreLayer: app/services - controllers stay thin and Lucid models hold no orchestration
conventions: Validators for all input
Migrations for every schema change
`node ace test` exits 0 with no tests, unlike pytest — a green test gate here does not mean tests exist

stacks.label: Elysia (Bun)
stacks.coreLayer: pure service modules - routes are only bindings
conventions: A `t.Object` schema on every route keeps type-safety end to end
`bun create elysia` currently emits a tsconfig with `moduleResolution: node10`, which current TypeScript rejects outright (TS5108) — fix it in the generated project, the typecheck gate is right

stacks.label: Expo (React Native)
stacks.coreLayer: src/services + src/hooks - screens are presentation only
conventions: expo-router for file-based navigation
Secrets NEVER go in app.json - use EAS secrets
Bump `android.versionCode`/`ios.buildNumber` at release; semver does not do it for you

stacks.label: React Native (bare)
stacks.coreLayer: src/services - shared JS; native modules stay thin bridges
conventions: Native versions (versionName / CFBundleShortVersionString) are synced by hand at release

stacks.label: Flutter
stacks.coreLayer: lib/src/domain + lib/src/data - widgets are presentation only
conventions: Pick one state management approach (Riverpod/Bloc) and apply it consistently
`const` constructors wherever possible - this is a real performance difference
The `+N` build number in pubspec.yaml is raised by hand for store releases

stacks.label: Ionic / Capacitor
stacks.coreLayer: the web service layer - native plugins are wrapped behind one adapter
conventions: Run `npx cap sync` after every native dependency change
An Ionic app is also an Angular/React/Vue app — Ionic wins primary because only it carries the native ignore rules, and the underlying framework stays as a secondary so its real gates still run

stacks.label: Android (Gradle)
stacks.coreLayer: domain/data modules (clean architecture) - Activities/Composables are UI only
conventions: `versionName` follows the semver; `versionCode` is a separate monotonic counter
Never commit a keystore or local.properties

stacks.label: Laravel
stacks.coreLayer: app/Services + app/Actions - controllers stay thin and Eloquent models hold no orchestration
conventions: Form Requests for validation, not `$request->validate()` sprinkled through controllers
Query through Eloquent scopes or query objects; keep raw SQL out of controllers
Long work goes to a queued Job, not the request cycle
Every schema change is a migration - never edit the database by hand

stacks.label: Symfony
stacks.coreLayer: services in src/Service plus Doctrine repositories - controllers are thin `__invoke`s
conventions: Autowiring and constructor injection; never pull from the container manually
Doctrine entities stay anaemic; logic lives in services/domain

stacks.label: CodeIgniter 4
stacks.coreLayer: app/Libraries + app/Models - controllers stay thin
conventions: CI4 Models for data access; validation via Model or Request rules
Explicit routes in Config/Routes.php; do not rely on auto-routing

appstarter's phpunit config asks for coverage, so `vendor/bin/phpunit` exits 1 with "OK, but there were issues!" when xdebug is absent — the tests passed. Install xdebug or run with --no-coverage in CI

stacks.label: Slim Framework
stacks.coreLayer: action classes plus services - routes are registration only
conventions: One class per action (single-action controllers)
PSR-15 middleware

stacks.label: WordPress (plugin / theme)
stacks.coreLayer: classes in includes/ - hook files only register actions and filters
conventions: Prefix EVERY function, option and table with the plugin slug - the global namespace is shared
Escape on output (`esc_html`/`esc_attr`), sanitise on input, nonce every form
The plugin version lives in the PHP header; sync it at release (see docs/VERSIONING.md)

`phpcs --standard=WordPress` exits 3 until wpcs is REGISTERED, not merely installed: `phpcs --config-set installed_paths vendor/wp-coding-standards/wpcs` (the composer plugin does it for you only when allow-plugins permits it to run)
wpcs pulls sniffs from PHPCSUtils and PHPCSExtra; a mismatched set fails with "Referenced sniff ... does not exist" rather than anything about your code

stacks.label: Django
stacks.coreLayer: services.py / custom managers per app - views stay thin and hold no business logic
conventions: Fat models or a service layer, thin views
`select_related`/`prefetch_related` to avoid N+1
Every model change ships with a committed migration

stacks.label: FastAPI
stacks.coreLayer: pure services/ modules - routers only validate and delegate
conventions: Pydantic models at the boundary; never leak ORM models into responses
Dependency injection via `Depends` for session and auth
`async def` endpoints only for genuinely async I/O - otherwise plain `def`

stacks.label: Flask
stacks.coreLayer: services/ modules - view functions stay thin
conventions: A blueprint per domain
Application factory (`create_app`), not a global app

stacks.label: Streamlit
stacks.coreLayer: pure modules importable without Streamlit - the UI script only calls them
conventions: `@st.cache_data` for expensive work
Secrets in `.streamlit/secrets.toml` (never committed)

stacks.label: Gin (Go)
stacks.coreLayer: internal/service packages - handlers bind, delegate and respond
conventions: `ShouldBindJSON` plus validator tags at the boundary
Middleware for cross-cutting concerns, not repeated per handler

stacks.label: Echo (Go)
stacks.coreLayer: internal/service packages - handlers stay thin
conventions: One central HTTPErrorHandler

stacks.label: Fiber (Go)
stacks.coreLayer: internal/service packages - handlers stay thin
conventions: Remember `c.Body()` is reused between requests - copy it before storing

stacks.label: chi / net-http (Go)
stacks.coreLayer: internal/service packages - `http.HandlerFunc` handlers stay thin
conventions: Stay `net/http`-compatible; that is the reason to pick chi

stacks.label: Axum (Rust)
stacks.coreLayer: domain/service modules - handlers are extractors plus delegation
conventions: Your own error type implementing `IntoResponse`
State through `State<T>`, never globals

stacks.label: Actix Web (Rust)
stacks.coreLayer: domain/service modules - handlers stay thin
conventions: `ResponseError` for domain errors
Never block a worker: CPU work goes to `web::block`

stacks.label: Rocket (Rust)
stacks.coreLayer: domain modules - routes are guards plus delegation
conventions: Request guards for auth, not manual checks in every route

stacks.label: Leptos (Rust, fullstack)
stacks.coreLayer: server functions (`#[server]`) - components stay presentational
conventions: Keep server-only code behind the `ssr` feature so it never reaches the WASM bundle
`cargo install cargo-leptos` fails on a clean Windows box — openssl-sys needs an OpenSSL that is not there. Use the prebuilt binary from the project's GitHub releases and check its published sha256

`cargo leptos new` refuses to run without a terminal ("IO error: not a terminal"), so in CI or an agent session clone the starter and resolve the cargo-generate placeholders yourself — including the `{% if %}` blocks, which are easy to miss

stacks.label: Spring Boot
stacks.coreLayer: @Service and @Repository - @RestControllers are thin and hold no business logic
conventions: Constructor injection (field injection is banned)
DTOs at the API boundary; never expose an @Entity directly
`@Transactional` on services, not controllers

stacks.label: Ktor (Kotlin)
stacks.coreLayer: service modules - routing is binding only
conventions: Compose features as plugins
Coroutines all the way; never `runBlocking` in a handler

stacks.label: Quarkus
stacks.coreLayer: @ApplicationScoped services - JAX-RS resources stay thin
conventions: Mind native-image limits (reflection needs explicit registration)

stacks.label: ASP.NET Core
stacks.coreLayer: the Application/Domain project - Controllers and minimal-API endpoints stay thin
conventions: Constructor DI; scoped lifetime for DbContext
Never return EF entities directly - use DTOs

stacks.label: Blazor
stacks.coreLayer: injected services - `.razor` components are presentation only
conventions: Know your render mode (Server vs WASM) before touching anything secret
Blazor and ASP.NET Core share the same csproj evidence, so this entry carries an explicit weight rather than a marker; ASP.NET Core remains a secondary stack and its gates still run

stacks.label: Ruby on Rails
stacks.coreLayer: app/services (service objects) - controllers stay thin and models hold no orchestration
conventions: Strong parameters in every controller
Avoid N+1 with `includes`
Schema changes only ever through migrations

stacks.label: Sinatra
stacks.coreLayer: pure service classes - route blocks stay thin
conventions: Modular style (`Sinatra::Base`), not the top-level DSL, for anything beyond a script

stacks.label: Phoenix (Elixir)
stacks.coreLayer: context modules (`MyApp.Accounts`) - controllers and LiveViews never touch Repo
conventions: One context per domain; the web layer calls contexts, not Ecto
Ecto changesets for all validation

stacks.label: Unity
stacks.coreLayer: plain C# classes (no MonoBehaviour) - MonoBehaviours are Unity glue only
conventions: No `Find`/`GetComponent` in `Update` - cache them in `Awake`
The version lives in ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset, set through Unity, not by script

stacks.label: Godot
stacks.coreLayer: standalone scripts (plain Resource/class) - node scripts are scene glue only
conventions: Signals for node-to-node communication, not direct path references

stacks.label: Terraform / OpenTofu
stacks.coreLayer: modules in modules/ - the root module is composition only
conventions: Remote state with locking - never commit local state
`*.tfvars` holds secrets: gitignored, not reviewed
Weighted below application frameworks on purpose: a repo that ships a compose file, Terraform or a chart usually has an app too, and that app is the primary stack

stacks.label: Helm chart
stacks.coreLayer: templates/ plus values.yaml - never hardcode a value in a template
conventions: `version` (the chart) and `appVersion` (the app) differ - scripts/version.mjs syncs both
Every new value gets a default in values.yaml
Weighted below application frameworks on purpose: a repo that ships a compose file, Terraform or a chart usually has an app too, and that app is the primary stack

stacks.label: Docker Compose
stacks.coreLayer: the application image - compose is local orchestration, not a place for logic
conventions: Pin image tags (never `latest`)
Secrets via a gitignored env file
Weighted below application frameworks on purpose: a repo that ships a compose file, Terraform or a chart usually has an app too, and that app is the primary stack
